mainTopic: Does plowing count toward a חזקה on land, how do רב and שמואל measure a חזקה, and how does a חזקה work in an orchard?
overview: The גמרא first shows that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא do not argue about plowing (ניר). Both agree plowing is not a חזקה. They argue about whether you need enough time for big crops or small crops. A ברייתא then shows that some Sages do count plowing, and רב חסדא identifies that view as רבי אחא. רב אשי reports that the great Sages of his generation agreed. רב נחמן explains both sides: an owner would not stay silent while others plow his land, or he is simply happy to get free plowing. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא answers the people of פום נהרא that plowing counts. רב נחמן בר יצחק objects that counting names proves nothing, since רב, שמואל, רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא all say plowing does not count. The גמרא then shows where רב and שמואל say this, and אביי explains how they differ, using a young date palm that gives three crops a year. Finally, the גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל's line about a grain field, and אביי learns from it that eating from ten different closely planted trees each year for three years is a חזקה even for the חכמים.

steps.title: If plowing counted, even one day would do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about whether plowing counts as a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If plowing counted, then even one day of plowing should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this, the גמרא suggested that the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about extra months at the start and end of the three years is really about plowing. Here it knocks that idea down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If plowing alone counted as using the field, you would not need months of activity at each end. One day of plowing would already be use of the field. Since both תנאים require months, the dispute cannot be about plowing.

phrases.english: Even one day should also be enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made just before this text, that the dispute is about plowing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that plowing is what separates רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If plowing counted, one day would be enough, so the months that both תנאים require would make no sense.

steps.title: Both agree plowing doesn't count; they argue about big versus small crops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. Everyone agrees plowing is not a חזקה. The argument is whether you need time for big crops or small crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees plowing is not a חזקה. Here the difference between them is big produce versus small produce.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the plowing explanation, the גמרא offers a different reason for the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל requires three months at each end, which is enough time to grow a big crop. רבי עקיבא requires only one month, which is enough for a small crop. Both agree that only real growing and eating of produce counts, not plowing.

keyTerms.meaning: proof of ownership through using land for three years
big produce, a crop that takes three months
small produce, a crop that takes one month

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא is about big crops versus small crops. It is not about plowing.

phrases.english: Rather, according to everyone,
plowing is not a חזקה;
and here, big produce
and small produce is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: Big produce takes about three months to grow and small produce about one month. That matches the three months versus one month at each end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים argue about whether plowing counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree plowing doesn't count. They argue about how much growing time is needed: big crop or small crop.

steps.title: A ברייתא: plowing is a debated point
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records two opinions. The first says plowing is not a חזקה, and 'some say' that it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: plowing is not a חזקה. And some say: it is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that there really is an opinion that plowing counts as a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said that in the dispute of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, everyone agrees plowing doesn't count. This ברייתא shows that elsewhere some Sages do hold that it counts. That opens a new discussion.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: plowing is not a חזקה.
And some say: this is a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִיר – אֵינוֹ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: is there an opinion that plowing counts?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute. The first opinion says plowing is not a חזקה, and 'some say' it is.

steps.title: Who is 'some say'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which Sage is behind the unnamed 'some say' opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'some say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to put a name on the unnamed opinion. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'some say' often stands for a known Sage. Naming him lets us link this opinion to other teachings of the same Sage.

phrases.english: Who is "some say"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unnamed opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the Sage who holds that plowing is a חזקה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי אחא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the 'some say' opinion belongs to רבי אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is רבי אחא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the name. The next step brings the ברייתא that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא links the unnamed view to רבי אחא. He relies on a ruling of רבי אחא in a different ברייתא that only makes sense if plowing counts.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אַחָא הִיא –
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: it is Rabbi Acha,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אַחָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'some say' opinion is רבי אחא.

steps.title: Proof: רבי אחא counts years of plowing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that plowing one year and sowing two, or the reverse, is not a חזקה. רבי אחא says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if he plowed it one year and sowed it two, or plowed it two years and sowed it one, it is not a חזקה. רבי אחא says: it is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source that proves רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases there are only three years if you count the plowing years. The first opinion says it is not a חזקה, so plowing doesn't count. רבי אחא says it is a חזקה, so he must count plowing, which matches the 'some say' view.

phrases.english: as it was taught: if he plowed it one year and sowed it two,
or plowed it two years and sowed it one,
it is not a חזקה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זוֹ חֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha says: this is a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נָרָהּ שָׁנָה, וּזְרָעָהּ שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's identification.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אחא holds plowing is a חזקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אחא counts years of plowing toward the three years.

steps.title: רב אשי: the great Sages said plowing counts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he asked all the great Sages of his generation, and they said plowing is a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I asked all the great Sages of the generation, and they told me plowing is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a report about how the halacha was being decided in his time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer just one תנא's opinion. רב אשי says the leading Sages of his day held that plowing counts. This pushes the halacha toward רבי אחא.

keyTerms.meaning: the great Sages of the generation

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁאֵלִית כׇּל גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I asked all the great men of the generation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לִי: נִיר – הֲרֵי זֶה חֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: and they said to me: plowing, this is a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁאֵלִית כׇּל גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the leading Sages for the view that plowing counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The great Sages of רב אשי's generation held that plowing is a חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This report is a big step toward deciding the practical halacha in favor of plowing counting.

steps.title: Why would plowing count?
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי asks רב נחמן for the reasoning of the view that plowing is a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said to רב נחמן: what is the reason of the one who says plowing is a חזקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion now turns from who holds each view to why they hold it. רב נחמן's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing produces nothing to eat, so it is not obvious why it shows ownership. רב ביבי wants the logic.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב בִּיבִי לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai said to Rav Nachman:
What is the reason of the one who says:
plowing is a חזקה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: נִיר הָוֵי חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the view just reported.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic for treating plowing as a חזקה.

steps.title: An owner would not stay silent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: people don't let someone plow their land and keep quiet.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person does not let others plow his land and stay silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the reason for the view that plowing counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה works because a real owner would protest if someone used his land. Plowing is a clear act on the land. If the owner said nothing for three years, it shows the land was sold to the plower.

phrases.english: A person does not usually
let others plow his land and stay silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא עֲבִיד אִינִישׁ דְּכָרְיבוּ לֵיהּ לְאַרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ביבי's first question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An owner would protest someone plowing his land. Silence shows he sold it.

steps.title: Why would plowing not count?
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי asks for the reasoning of the other side, which says plowing is not a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of the one who says plowing is not a חזקה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי now asks about the opposite view. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Given the strong logic in step 9, it is hard to see why anyone would disagree. So he asks what the other side is thinking.

phrases.english: And what is the reason of the one who says:
plowing is not a חזקה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: נִיר לָא הָוֵי חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning of the opposite view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic for not treating plowing as a חזקה.

steps.title: The owner is happy to get free plowing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: the owner thinks, 'Let every clump of earth go into the plow.' He is glad someone is plowing his field for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says to himself: let every single clump get into the plow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains why some hold that plowing does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing only helps the land. It takes nothing from the owner. So his silence may just mean he is happy for the free work, planning to sow and harvest himself. It does not prove he sold the land.
steps.confusionAlert: The owner's silence is not agreement that the land was sold. On this view, it only shows he is glad for free work on his field.

phrases.english: He says to himself:
every single clump for the plow,
let it go into it.
phrases.notes: In other words, the more of my land he plows, the better for me.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵימָר אָמַר: כֹּל שִׁיבָּא וְשִׁיבָּא דִּכְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ביבי's second question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner keeps quiet because free plowing helps him, so his silence proves nothing.

steps.title: פום נהרא asks for a ruling
steps.stepSummary: The people of פום נהרא send a question to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא: is plowing a חזקה or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of פום נהרא sent to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא: Teach us, our master, is plowing a חזקה or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A community asks for a practical ruling. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides have reasonable logic, so a real community needs to know which way to rule in actual cases.

phrases.english: The people of Pum Nahara sent
to Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda:
Let our master teach us:
plowing, is it a חזקה,
or is it not a חזקה?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי פּוּם נַהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from reasoning to asking for a practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halacha: does plowing count as a חזקה?

steps.title: Ruling: plowing is a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא answers that רבי אחא and all the great Sages of the generation say plowing is a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: רבי אחא and all the great Sages of the generation say plowing is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The practical ruling is given: plowing counts as a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer combines the two sources we saw: רבי אחא from the ברייתא and the great Sages from רב אשי's report. The next step questions whether listing great names really settles the matter.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא ruled for פום נהרא that plowing counts as a חזקה, relying on רבי אחא and the great Sages. The reason is that an owner would not stay silent while others plow his land. But the very next step challenges this ruling.

phrases.english: He said to them: Rabbi Acha
and all the great men of the generation say:
plowing, this is a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ, רַבִּי אַחָא וְכׇל גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from פום נהרא in step 12; step 14 then challenges this answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Plowing counts as a חזקה, following רבי אחא and the great Sages of the generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical answer the people of פום נהרא were given, and it becomes the target of רב נחמן בר יצחק's challenge in the next step.

steps.title: Counting great names proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects to the report that all the great Sages say plowing is a חזקה. He names four great Sages who say it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Is it a big deal to count up names? Look, רב and שמואל in בבל, and רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא in ארץ ישראל, all say plowing is not a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the answer from step 13. Listing famous Sages does not settle the question, because just as many famous Sages hold the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 tried to win the argument by pointing to a crowd of great Sages. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers with his own list of four giants, from both בבל and ארץ ישראל, who say plowing is not a חזקה. So the matter is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: To count up people, meaning to list names of Sages
Proof of ownership that comes from using land without protest

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is a different person from רב נחמן in steps 9 and 11, and from רב נחמן בר רב חסדא in step 13.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Is it a big deal to count up names?!
phrases.notes: He is mocking the answer in step 13, which pointed to 'all the great Sages of the generation.'

phrases.english: Look, Rav and Shmuel in Babylonia,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva in Eretz Yisrael,
say: Plowing is not a ḥazaka!

steps.triggerLanguage: רְבוּתָא לְמִיחְשַׁב גַּבְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all the great Sages hold plowing is a חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Just as many great Sages hold the opposite, so counting names proves nothing.

steps.title: The source showing רב holds plowing is not a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The view of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא comes from the משנה. רב's view comes from his teaching that a חזקה takes three years 'from day to day,' which leaves plowing out.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, the source is our משנה. Where do we see it from רב? רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, but the חכמים say a field's חזקה is three years, from day to day. What does 'from day to day' leave out? Doesn't it leave out plowing, which does not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the list in step 14 by showing where each Sage says this. Here it shows the sources for רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא already hold this in the משנה. רב says the halacha follows the חכמים, who require three complete years 'from day to day.' The גמרא reads those words as cutting out plowing, so plowing alone does not start the count.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Meaning, where is the source?
From day to day; three full years

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – מַתְנִיתִין הִיא;
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva — it is our mishna;
Rav — what is the source?
As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that a few months of use in the first and third years is enough.

phrases.english: but the Rabbis say:
its ḥazaka is three years, from day to day.
'From day to day' comes to exclude what?
Is it not to exclude plowing, which does not count?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב – מַאי הִיא? דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources behind the names listed in step 14
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds plowing is not a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that a חזקה is three years 'from day to day'

steps.title: The source showing שמואל holds plowing is not a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the halacha follows the חכמים, who require three harvests. Plowing is not a harvest, so it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see it from שמואל? רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is the view of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, but the חכמים say there is no חזקה until he harvests three date crops, picks three grape crops, and gathers three olive crops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where שמואל holds that plowing is not a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל measures a חזקה by actual harvests, three of them. Plowing produces no harvest, so by his measure it cannot be a חזקה.

phrases.english: Shmuel — what is the source?
As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva,
but the Rabbis say:
not until he harvests three date crops,
and picks three grape crops,
and gathers three olive crops.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל – מַאי הִיא? דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 15, now for שמואל
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל holds plowing is not a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement that a חזקה requires three harvests

steps.title: How do רב and שמואל differ?
steps.stepSummary: רב speaks of three years and שמואל of three harvests. The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what practical difference there is between the way רב and the way שמואל describe a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most fields give one crop a year, so three years and three harvests usually come out the same. The question looks for a case where the two measures give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two sources just brought
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רב's 'three years' and שמואל's 'three harvests'

steps.title: אביי: a young date palm that gives fruit three times a year
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference shows up with a young date palm, which gives three crops in one year.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The difference between them is a young date palm, which gives fruit three times in one year.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a tree that gives three crops in a single year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this tree, three harvests can happen within one year. By שמואל's wording of three harvests, that could be enough. By רב's wording of three full years, it would not be.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל hold that plowing is not a חזקה. They differ only in how to measure a חזקה: by time (רב) or by harvests (שמואל).

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A young date palm is the difference between them —
which produces fruit three times in a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דֶּקֶל נַעֲרָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A young date palm that gives three crops in one year: three harvests but not three years

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the time rule is about a grain field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי ישמעאל from the משנה: the time rule for a חזקה applies to a grain field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: When is this said? In a grain field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up אביי's lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל limits the time rule to a שדה הלבן, a field of grain. The משנה goes on to say that an orchard works differently: harvesting its different fruits can count, even at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? In what case does the rule apply?
A 'white field,' meaning a grain field with no trees

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
In what case is this said —
in a white field.
phrases.notes: A 'white field' is a grain field. The משנה goes on to say that an orchard follows a different rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time rule of the משנה is about a grain field; an orchard is treated differently.

steps.title: אביי: eating from different trees each year still counts
steps.stepSummary: From רבי ישמעאל, אביי learns a rule for the חכמים. If thirty trees are planted closely and he ate from ten different trees each year for three years, that is a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From רבי ישמעאל we can learn about the חכמים. If someone had thirty trees, planted ten per בית סאה, and he ate the fruit of ten in this year, ten in this year, and ten in this year, that is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses רבי ישמעאל's view to work out how the חכמים would rule in an orchard case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל lets different crops harvested at different times join together into a חזקה. אביי says even the חכמים, who require three years, agree that eating from different trees each year joins together. The trees are close enough to count as one field.

keyTerms.meaning: We can learn; we can infer
An area of land big enough to plant one סאה of seed

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a חזקה in an orchard does not need the same trees every year. Ten different, closely planted trees each year for three years is enough.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From Rabbi Yishmael we can learn about the Rabbis:
phrases.notes: 'The Rabbis' are the Sages who disagree with רבי ישמעאל and require three years even for an orchard.

phrases.english: if he had thirty trees —
planted ten per beit se'a;
and he ate the fruit of ten in this year,
and ten in this year,
and ten in this year —
this is a ḥazaka.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל נִשְׁמַע לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a rule for the חכמים out of רבי ישמעאל's statement in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating from ten different, closely planted trees in each of three years creates a חזקה on all thirty trees.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even the stricter view of the חכמים judges an orchard as one whole field, not tree by tree.
